summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/72)

data.turoyo: ḤD. Yaho, lo+ḥowənwa. Səmlan ruḥayna mu+bayto.
data.translation: HD. For goodness’ sake, they would not host. We made ourselves at home.

rationale: First I Infectum-wa box; compact habitual refusal to host, followed by the travellers' response.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/224)

data.turoyo: ḤD. Áydarbo? Yawo, naqlawoṯe, domaṇṇux mede, fayšíwayna larwal, lo+ḥowə̀nwaylan hən maq+qәryawoṯe. Dəmxíwayna hawxa dəmmina bu+zaboqo.
data.translation: How? For goodness’ sake, sometimes, let me tell you something, we used to stay outside, some of the villages wouldn’t host us. We would sleep, so to speak, on the street.

rationale: I Infectum-wa example with an overt village subject and first-person plural guests; refusal leads to sleeping outside.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/227)

data.turoyo: I. Yani bu+zabnawo káfnowa, áydarbo an+noše ḥowənwa dayfe?
data.translation: Like, at that time there was a famine, how would people host guests?

rationale: I Infectum-wa with explicit guests as a zero-marked object, complementing suffix-coded guests.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 12/4)

data.turoyo: Azzən l qriṯo, azze u malla l bayto, omər: “ḥwawullan.” Əmmi: “ʕAl aʕ ʕayne, toxu, itawu.”
data.translation: begaben sie sich in's Dorf. Der Molla trat in ein Haus und bat: »Beherbergt uns«. »Recht gern«, war die Antwort, »kommt und setzt euch«.

rationale: First I Imperativ box; plural hosts and first-person plural lodgers; complete hospitality request and reply.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 58/46)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Šquləx ʕaṣro quġš w ḥwayli adlalyo." Əmmo: "Ṭrowe."
data.translation: "Da hast du zehn Piaster, beherberge mich diese Nacht." "Gut!" antwortete sie

rationale: I Imperativ with feminine host and first-person guest; payment and tonight establish a lodging request.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (113/182)

data.turoyo: "Hay aman d axil, ya barṯi, ḥwayli, kəbʕono, d əṯyono lawġul." Əmmo: "Abadan i mkaniye latla!" Omər səmla w lo səmla, lo ḥuyola.
data.translation: Erbarmen, meine Tochter! Laß mich ein, ich will hereinkommen. - Ganz unmöglich! - Was die alte auch anstellte, sie ließ sie nicht herein.

rationale: I Imperativ ḥwayli in an admission request, contrasted immediately with a negative Preterit response.

data.turoyo: Aḥna sidan u ḥa, d kḥuwele sawal, mənayye kuwalle ʕwone, mənayye ʕeze w mənayye tawroṯo.
data.translation: Wer bei uns Tiere hält ... Manche haben Schafe, manche Ziegen und manche Kühe.

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; livestock keeping extends the already attested housing of goats; retain as participant/context extension.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 33/50)

data.turoyo: Azze lu balad dag gurǧ, ʕabər s ḥḏo pire, omər: “Lo kḥuwatli, pire, adlalyo gabəx?” Əmmo: “Ma ʕayni, gḥawyallox.”
data.translation: und begab sich in das Land der Gurdsch. Dort trat er bei einer alten Frau ein und fragte sie: »Willst du mich nicht diese Nacht bei dir beherbergen?« »Recht gern will ich dich beherbergen«, gab sie ihm zur Antwort.

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; second-person request and first-person feminine promise in one compact aligned exchange.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 83/21)

data.turoyo: Azze sə ḥḏo pire, taʕalṯo. Omər: "Taʕalṯo!" Əmmo: "Ha?" Omər: "Lə kḥovət ono w ḥoṯi adlalyo?" Əmmo: "ʕAl aʕ ʕayne."
data.translation: Dort ging er zu einer alten Füchsin und sagte: "Füchsin!" "Ja!" "Willst du nicht mich und meine Schwester diese Nacht beherbergen?" "Zu Diensten!" antwortete sie.

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; coordinated free-pronoun and noun object without a personal object suffix; retain v spelling.

data.turoyo: I=naqla d maḥrawle i=niyayḏe ʕal i=kačke, i=kačke ṣxəlla u=tarʕo quma w mlela bəṯre d u=tarʕo kefe w haw ḥwela u=faqqa.
data.translation: Als er solche schlimmen Absichten auf das Mädchen gefaßt hatte, verschloß das Mädchen die Tür vor ihm, füllte hinter der Türe Steine auf und ließ den Schulmeister nicht herein.

rationale: Thin Preterit/1 cell; barring the schoolmaster after blocking the door. haw can be the negative no-longer particle; no missing negative is supplied.

data.turoyo: L u goranawo hiye ste, i naqqa d kobəʕ motela l s i ḥawwe, am məštaʕyone ḥrene koṯən l qamuṯe, kəmḥarbi aʕme, l boyi d lo maḥwela xayifo.
data.translation: Wenn er nun die "Mutter" in dem "Häuschen" unterbringen will, treten die anderen Spieler ihm entgegen und kämpfen mit ihm, damit er sie nicht so schnell dort unterbringen kann.

rationale: Thin III Infectum/1 cell; technical game target and competing players prevent housing the horn quickly.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/518)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr gbodən naqla ḥreto, gqorən l ḥḏoḏe. U ḥa, d maḥwela, hiye qamayto koqore.
data.translation: Dann fängt man ein neues Spiel an. Sie "rufen" einer den anderen, und der, welcher die "Mutter" im "Häuschen" unterbringt, "ruft" zuerst.

rationale: Thin III Infectum/1 cell; relative clause identifies the player who houses the horn and calls first.

summary: I hospitality has unmarked nominal guests, free coordinated objects, fronted/resumed guests, and personal object suffixes. A suffix on a transitive hosting verb denotes the lodger, not automatically an experiencer.
Habitual refusal to host supplies the missing I Infectum-wa; plural ḥwawullan and feminine ḥwayli supply I Imperativ. Existing II and technical III meanings remain unchanged.
The embedded Nisane transcript is editorial evidence on an existing example, not a third independently indexed Infectum example. Preserve it and do not count an unnumbered note as a quotation.
In 88/245 haw before ḥwela can express no longer, as haw also negates admission in 81/54. The barricading context agrees with exclusion; no lo/lə is invented.
Hospitality collocations with guests are ordinary object combinations and are already expressed by the inherited sense; no new idiom or abstract acceptance sense is warranted.
Does JTM 1.1/72 assert keeping/rearing animals or only housing them? Confirm the function of -le in kḥuwele.
Confirm second-person agreement and v/w spelling in kḥovət with feminine taʕalṯo (PrS 83/21); do not infer an invariant gender form from one spelling.
Confirm the source reading of haw ḥwela (88/245) as negative no longer. The context supports exclusion, and no extra negation has been inserted.
Compare k- in the inherited Nisane note with source g̊- at MAC NE Interview 2/225; retain both until edition/transcription provenance is checked.
Correct the truncated noun “Flughor”.
rationale: The final n is missing from the German noun Flughorn. The example and supplied translation explicitly refer to a horn driven into a little house in a game.

summary: Housing livestock can denote keeping it in the domestic economy; ownership or rearing is not independently established as a separate sense.
Hosts may be villages/households or animals in fables; guests may be object suffixes or unmarked coordinated expressions. Admission to a house remains within the inherited 'ins Haus aufnehmen' gloss.
